extracted.intended_audience: 9th-10th grade English teachers and curriculum planners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards-aligned guidance, rubrics, assessments, and lesson-plan suggestions for teaching 9th–10th grade writing (argumentative, informative/explanatory, and narrative) under the Common Core State Standards. Includes criterion-level scoring descriptors and classroom activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, argumentative, and compelling thesis statement (rubric level: Excellent: "Clear, argumentative, and compelling thesis statement"; descending levels indicate less clarity, vagueness, or absence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment rubric differentiates performance (Excellent/Good/Satisfactory/Needs Improvement). Lesson plan includes a "Thesis Statement Workshop" (teach characteristics of effective theses; practice creating theses). Emphasize clarity, specificity, and arguable claim; tie thesis to overall organization and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides well-reasoned arguments with varied and strong evidence (Excellent: "Provides well-reasoned arguments with varied and strong evidence"; lower levels indicate sufficient, shallow, or weak/no evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring tiers emphasize depth of reasoning and quality/variety of evidence. Lesson activities include evaluating evidence (strong vs. weak examples), requiring students to integrate textual and real-world evidence, and drafting with emphasis on reasoning chains linking evidence to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges and refutes counterarguments (Excellent: "Skillfully acknowledges and refutes counterarguments"; lower levels show partial acknowledgement, mere mention, or ignoring counterarguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric rewards both recognition of opposing views and effective refutation. Lesson plan suggests role-play or debates to practice acknowledging/refuting viewpoints and building rebuttals; peer review can check for presence and quality of counterargument treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and Coherence (for Arguments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas are logically organized and transitions are smooth, enhancing the argument (Excellent: "Ideas are logically organized and transitions are smooth"; lower tiers show awkward transitions, attempted organization, or disorganization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric links organization to argumentative effectiveness. Classroom guidance: teach paragraph structure, use of transitions, and organization strategies that make reasoning clear; include drafting and peer review to improve coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Coherence (Informative/Explanatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is clear, logical, and well-structured, guiding the reader through complex ideas (Excellent: "exceptionally clear, logical, and well-structured" down to "often unclear and lacks a logical structure").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for clarity of exposition and logical flow. Lesson suggestions: model expository structures, scaffold introductions and conclusions, and practice organizing multi-paragraph explanations. Peer review and revision focus on eliminating lapses in logic or structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides in-depth examination of aspects of the topic with thorough analysis and evidence (Excellent: "in-depth examination... thorough analysis"; lower tiers show limited or superficial coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric prioritizes comprehensive, analytical treatment over superficial summary. Classroom guidance: research and note-taking sessions, require students to synthesize multiple sources, and prompt analysis (not just reporting) of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Evidence (Informative/Explanatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a wide variety of relevant and detailed evidence to support the examination (Excellent: "wide variety of relevant and detailed evidence"; lower tiers show limited, generic, or irrelevant evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include appropriate selection, integration, and citation of evidence. Lesson plan: teach paraphrasing, quoting, and citing; practice integrating sources smoothly into analysis; provide exemplars of strong vs. weak evidence usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Structure (Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits a well-structured plot, including a strong beginning, development, and satisfying conclusion (Excellent: "well-structured plot... strong beginning, development, and satisfying conclusion"; lower tiers lack development or coherent conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric emphasizes exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution. Lessons: plot development exercises, use of story maps or prompts, and drafting sequences to ensure clear beginning/middle/end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are fully developed with distinct voices, actions, and motivations (Excellent: "Characters are fully developed"; lower tiers show limited depth or stereotypical characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for distinct voices, motivations, and believable actions. Classroom activities: character-creation workshops, exploring desires/fears/flaws, and revision exercises focused on deepening characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Dialogue and Details (Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses engaging dialogue and specific details to convey experiences and events vividly (Excellent: "engaging dialogue and specific details"; lower tiers have forced, sparse, or absent dialogue/details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric rewards sensory detail and dialogue that advances plot or reveals character. Lessons: practice writing realistic dialogue, sensory-detail exercises, and peer feedback on vividness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to navigate sources, distinguish credible from questionable sources, and integrate research ("skilled researcher... distinguishing between the credible and the questionable. Their bibliography is formatted flawlessly, and their writing seamlessly integrates these sources").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes classroom Research and Note-taking lesson (30 minutes), instruction on reliable sources, and practice synthesizing evidence. Expect assessment of source credibility, correct bibliography formatting, and seamless integration of sources into argument or exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Process Understanding (Revision and Peer Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding that writing is a process: drafting, peer review, accepting feedback, and revising to improve ("First drafts are just that—first drafts... final drafts show a marked improvement").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lesson structure includes Drafting and Peer Review, with revision cycles and explicit opportunities for feedback. Rubric/assessment should reward evidence of revision and improvement between drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Language and Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Command of grade-appropriate language and conventions: varied sentence structures, precise word choice, adherence to grammar rules, with occasional deliberate stylistic departures ("command of grade-appropriate language and conventions... adhere to grammar rules... may break a rule here and there for stylistic purposes").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors evaluate grammar, mechanics, diction, sentence variety, and stylistic control. Classroom work: instruction on conventions, targeted mini-lessons (e.g., semicolons), and editing exercises; rubrics should distinguish precision and maturity of language use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and Achieving Writing Goals (Metacognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students set personal writing goals (e.g., enhancing descriptive language, mastering semicolons, experimenting with voice) and pursue measurable improvement ("sets personal writing goals... accepts that perfection isn’t the goal, but progress is").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reflection activities, goal-setting conferences, and self-assessment checklists. Assessors may consider documented goals and evidence of progress toward those goals in scored submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Technology for Production and Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploring technology to produce, publish, and collaborate on writing projects (standards note: "exploring the use of technology to produce and publish writing as well as to collaborate on projects").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lesson suggestions include using digital platforms for drafting, peer review, multimedia publication, and collaborative documents. Assessment can include quality of digital publication, appropriate use of tools, and evidence of collaborative revision.
